title: The client says: “Use my Gmail today”
scenario: A long-standing client emails from their normal corporate account saying their document system is down. They ask you to send a confidential customer file to a personal Gmail address “just for today” so a deadline is not missed.

answers.A: Hold the file until the client can provide an approved alternative channel or your security/privacy team authorizes one.
answers.B: Send it because the request came from the client’s real mailbox and the personal address belongs to the same person.
answers.C: Verify the request through a known contact and keep the file inside approved secure channels; escalate if the client’s normal system is unavailable.

explanation: A real relationship does not make an unapproved data destination safe. Compromised mailboxes and genuine users under pressure can both create risky requests.
proTip: Trust the relationship; still verify the destination and the data-handling rule.
